subject: Post-call: Nightingale latency targets & bakeoff next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Karen Mitchell <karen@nightingale.ai>, Rahul Sethi <rahul@nightingale.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next steps for latency bakeoff

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap of agreed items and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the bakeoff: 

Summary / targets you called out:
- p95 end-to-end (in-region): target = 120 ms
- p99 end-to-end (in-region): target = 320 ms
- Traffic envelope: average 250 req/s with 1–2% spikes to 800 req/s for 30s, mostly short prompts (~128 tokens) with occasional long-form (1–2k tokens) batch transforms (about 5% of traffic)
- Streaming: client-side expects chunked streaming for partial responses; we should validate stall behavior at concurrency >= 80

What Redwood will do next:
- Provide SLO checklist + test harness and a suggested traffic profile (attached).
- Run an initial hosted bakeoff against your sample traffic (in-region) and share p95/p99 deltas vs incumbent.
- Validate streaming behavior at 20/50/80 concurrent users, and measure tail under burst traffic.

Asks from Nightingale (please confirm):
1) Confirm the traffic CSV format (attached) is accurate for typical weekday load and spike windows.
2) Any IP allowlist / egress constraints we should use for the bakeoff?
3) If you have a sample corpus for the long-form transforms, please attach or point us to a Drive link.

Proposed schedule:
- 9/16: Redwood infra prep & ingest traffic profile
- 9/17: Hosted bakeoff (two runs: baseline + tuned caching/quantization)
- 9/18: Results briefing and next decision call

Attachments: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (SLO checklist + test matrix), sample-network-trace.txt (what we request for request-path validation), nightingale-traffic-envelope.csv (example you can confirm)

If this looks right I’ll lock the run times and loop in our infra team.

—Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa — recap looks good and the attached traffic CSV matches our telemetry for core production. A few clarifications: 

- Confirming p95 120 ms / p99 320 ms are end-to-end (client -> our app -> model -> client) including TLS handshake overhead.
- For spikes, the 800 req/s is a client-visible spike; behind our proxy that maps to ~950 requests/s. We can provide a short window of live traffic capture for your team.
- Streaming: we stream partial tokens every ~150ms; we want to ensure token chunks arrive without >250ms stalls during steady-state, and that stalls during burst windows are graceful.

IP / network notes:
- We can provide a single egress CIDR for the test. We prefer TLS mutual auth for the bakeoff; can Redwood support client certs?

Corpus: uploading a sanitized sample set to Drive now — link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=nightingale-sample-corpus

Forwarding Nightingale's confirmation and ask for engineering scope. Key asks: mTLS support for the test, streaming stall tolerances (<=250ms), and traffic spike of ~950 req/s behind their proxy. 

Can you please: 
- Confirm whether hosted Redwood can meet p95=120ms / p99=320ms for the stated profile, and what tuning steps we should run during the two bakeoff passes (baseline + tuned).
- Share a minimal test plan (tools, expected metrics, telemetry hooks we need to collect: per-request latencies with request-id, streaming chunk timings, CPU/GPU utilization, NVLink stats).
- Advise whether any model quantization or server-side batching profiles are recommended for the long-form 1–2k token transforms.

Ideally have a short write-up by EOD 9/16 so I can confirm the run window with Nightingale.

On Sep 14, 2026, Karen Mitchell <karen@nightingale.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Vanessa — recap looks good and the attached traffic CSV matches our telemetry for core production. ...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + proposed next steps for latency bakeoff (Nightingale)

High-level feasibility note from infra: short answer — yes, hosted can meet these numbers with the right config. Details and caveats below.

Assumptions we’re validating:
- Model: 70B-parameter family-ish (you haven’t given exact model yet), mixed short and rare long sequences.
- Avg token lengths ~128 for 95% of requests; 5% are long-form up to 2k tokens.
- In-region network RTT <= 10–20 ms (we need their ci/net trace to confirm).

Baseline run (what to expect):
- With continuous batching disabled (per-request routing), p95 will likely be ~90–140 ms for short prompts; p99 can balloon due to GPU scheduling and the long-form mix — expect 350–500 ms in worst-case for baseline.

Tuning pass (we’ll enable):
1) Prefix & KV caching for repeated prompts — this reduces avg tokens processed and lowers tail.
2) Workload-aware batching for short prompts (continuous batching with a 10–20 ms batching window) to improve throughput without adding much latency for p95.
3) Model quantization profile (4-bit/8-bit mixed path) for long-form transforms to keep GPU per-token latency lower; expected p99 improvement ~15–25% depending on accuracy trade-offs.
4) Streaming chunk optimization: emit smaller initial chunk quickly (first-token optimization) then steady-state larger chunks to keep client-side stall below 250 ms.

Telemetry hooks we need for the run:
- Per-request: request-id, start_ts, first_token_ts, last_token_ts, total_tokens, and final HTTP status.
- Streaming: timestamps for each chunk boundary, chunk_size_tokens, network_send_time.
- Host metrics: GPU utilization, async queue length, NVLink throughput, host CPU % and network egress.

Network / security: we support mTLS for test endpoints; please provide cert bundle and egress CIDR.

Test tooling: we recommend k6 (for concurrency envelope) + a small harness that validates chunk arrival timing (we can share ours).

Next: Karthik and I will draft a concise test runbook and a list of preconfigured run permutations (baseline, caching on, quantized model) by 2026-09-16 17:00 PT. That should give you enough to approve the 9/17 run.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Karen Mitchell <karen@nightingale.ai>, Rahul Sethi <rahul@nightingale.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, ProcureOps <procure@nightingale.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Confirmed: 9/17 bakeoff recap + mutual action plan

Hi Karen / Rahul — thanks for the quick turnaround and the corpus link. Follow-up with final plan and what to expect from Redwood during the hosted bakeoff tomorrow (9/17):

What we will run (two passes):
A) Baseline: no prefix caching, default FP/quant settings, continuous batching disabled. Purpose: replicate current provider baseline and surface scheduling tail.
B) Tuned: prefix/KV caching enabled, continuous batching with 15 ms window for short prompts, mixed 4-bit quantization for long-form transforms, streaming first-token optimization enabled. Purpose: show achievable improvements and trade-offs.

Telemetry & artifacts we will deliver after each run:
- p50/p95/p99 latency histograms (end-to-end) and per-stage breakdown (network, model, streaming chunk gaps).
- GPU/host utilization traces, NVLink summaries, and request-id level logs for 0.1% sample.
- Short screen recording of streaming chunk timings for a sample session.

Mutual action plan / decision checkpoints:
1) Nightingale to supply mTLS certs and the final traffic CSV by 9/16 EOD (received — thanks).
2) Redwood to complete infra prep and ingest traffic by 9/16 end of day (done).
3) Bakeoff runs 9/17 (baseline at 09:00 PT, tuned at 14:00 PT).
4) Results briefing 9/18 at 10:00 PT (calendar invite going out).

Acceptance criteria we’ll use for a green decision:
- Hosted p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 320 ms for the stated in-region profile without manual per-request overrides OR a documented mitigation (fallback routing or limited model variant) with acceptable UX implications.
- Streaming chunk stalls <= 250 ms steady-state at concurrency levels up to 80.
- No data egress anomalies and mTLS validated.

If the tuned pass meets the acceptance criteria, we’ll prepare a short SLA proposal and cost estimate for the Dedicated/Reserved deployment that matches their traffic envelope.

See attached report template and the runbook link: https://docsend.com/view/nightingale-bakeoff-plan

Thanks — see you on the results call.

—Vanessa
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
